question: Which welding process is most suitable for joining thin gauge stainless steel components requiring minimal distortion and high aesthetic quality?
options: Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SMAW)
Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW/TIG)
Flux-Cored Arc Welding (FCAW)
Submerged Arc Welding (SAW)

question: When performing a destructive bend test on a butt weld, a crack appearing on the tension face that is greater than what length is considered a failure according to standard welding codes?
options: 1/8 inch (3mm)
1/4 inch (6mm)
3/8 inch (9mm)
1/2 inch (12mm)

question: In AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code, what is the minimum preheat temperature required for welding A514 steel with a thickness greater than 2.5 inches?
A welder is producing a GMAW weld and notices excessive spatter and a convex bead profile. Which combination of parameter adjustments would most likely correct this issue?
options: Decrease voltage and increase wire feed speed
Increase voltage and decrease wire feed speed
Increase both voltage and wire feed speed
Decrease both voltage and wire feed speed

question: What is the primary purpose of post-weld heat treatment (PWHT) applied to pressure vessel welds?
options: To increase the hardness of the weld metal
To relieve residual stresses and reduce hydrogen-induced cracking susceptibility
To improve the visual appearance of the weld bead
To increase the carbon content of the heat-affected zone

question: In plasma arc cutting, the difference between transferred arc and non-transferred arc modes is best described as:
options: In transferred arc mode, the arc is established between the electrode and the nozzle; in non-transferred, between electrode and workpiece
In transferred arc mode, the arc is established between the electrode and the workpiece; in non-transferred, between electrode and nozzle
Transferred arc uses a pilot arc only, while non-transferred uses a main arc only
There is no functional difference between the two modes

question: Which type of weld joint discontinuity is characterized by an unfused area between weld passes or between weld metal and base metal that does not extend to the surface?
options: Porosity
Incomplete fusion (lack of fusion)
Undercut
Overlap

question: When interpreting a welding symbol, a weld symbol placed below the reference line indicates:
options: The weld is on the far side of the joint
The weld is on the arrow side of the joint
The weld is a back weld
The weld requires full penetration

question: Which non-destructive examination (NDE) method is most effective for detecting subsurface planar discontinuities such as lack of fusion in a thick-section weld?
options: Liquid penetrant testing (PT)
Magnetic particle testing (MT)
Ultrasonic testing (UT)
Visual inspection (VT)

question: In oxyfuel gas welding, the carburizing (reducing) flame is identified by which characteristic?
options: A sharp, well-defined inner cone with no intermediate feather
An intermediate feather between the inner cone and outer envelope
A large, soft outer envelope with a barely visible inner cone
A loud hissing sound and blue coloration throughout the flame

question: According to the heat input formula used in welding engineering, if voltage is 28V, current is 180A, and travel speed is 6 inches per minute (converted appropriately), what is the heat input in kJ/inch?
options: Approximately 25.2 kJ/inch
Approximately 50.4 kJ/inch
Approximately 12.6 kJ/inch
Approximately 8.4 kJ/inch

question: What is the primary metallurgical reason that austenitic stainless steels can experience sensitization in the heat-affected zone during welding?
options: Chromium carbides precipitate at grain boundaries, depleting adjacent areas of chromium below 12%
Nickel carbides form in the weld metal reducing corrosion resistance
The ferrite content increases above 20% causing stress corrosion cracking
Carbon diffuses into the weld metal causing embrittlement

question: In FCAW-G (gas-shielded flux-cored arc welding), which shielding gas mixture provides the best balance between arc stability, penetration, and reduced spatter for welding carbon steel?
options: 100% Argon
75% Argon / 25% CO2
50% Argon / 50% Helium

question: A fabricator is required to qualify a new Welding Procedure Specification (WPS) per ASME Section IX. Which of the following changes would require a complete re-qualification of the procedure?
options: Changing the shielding gas flow rate by 5 CFH
Changing the base metal P-Number from P-1 to P-8
Changing the interpass temperature within the qualified range
Changing the weld bead sequence within the same joint design

question: When performing radiographic testing (RT) of a weld, the image quality indicator (IQI) or penetrameter is placed on the source side of the weld. What does this placement verify?
options: The geometric unsharpness of the radiographic image
That the required sensitivity and density of the radiograph meet acceptance criteria
The distance from the source to the film
The travel speed used during welding
